subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Build confidence with numbers, patterns, algebraic reasoning, and problem-solving.

topics.title: Whole Numbers & Place Value
topics.summary: Understand place value, ordering, and operations with large numbers.
objectives: Read and write large whole numbers up to millions.
Compare and order integers correctly.
Apply the four basic arithmetic operations.
topics.lesson: Whole numbers are numbers used for counting, including 0, 1, 2, 3, and onwards. Place value dictates the worth of a digit based on its exact position (units, tens, hundreds, thousands, millions).
topics.example: In 4,582, the digit 4 represents 4,000, 5 represents 500, 8 represents 80, and 2 represents 2.

questions.q: What is the value of 7 in 3,742?
questions.explain: The 7 occupies the hundreds position, yielding 700.

questions.q: Which number is greatest among 2,908, 2,980, and 2,890?
questions.explain: Comparing digits from left to right, 2,980 is the largest.

topics.title: Fractions & Equivalent Fractions
topics.summary: Learn how fractions represent parts of a whole and how to find equivalent fractions.
objectives: Identify numerators and denominators.
Recognise and compute equivalent fractions.
Compare proper and improper fractions.
topics.lesson: A fraction represents a proportion of a whole. The numerator above the line specifies parts considered, while the denominator below specifies total equal divisions.
topics.example: In 3/4, the numerator is 3 and denominator is 4, representing three out of four equal parts.

questions.explain: The denominator is the bottom integer: 5.

subjects.name: Intermediate Science
subjects.description: Explore living organisms, matter, energy, and environmental sustainability.

topics.title: Living & Non-Living Things
topics.summary: Identify characteristics of living things and classify matter.
objectives: Distinguish biotic factors from abiotic objects.
List life processes (Movement, Respiration, Nutrition, etc.).
Classify everyday specimens.
topics.lesson: Living things carry out life processes such as nutrition, respiration, growth, excretion, sensitivity, movement, and reproduction. Non-living items lack these independent biological characteristics.
topics.example: A sprouting mango tree is living because it undergoes growth and cellular respiration. A stone is non-living.

questions.q: Which of these is a living organism?
questions.explain: A mango tree grows and performs life processes.

subjects.name: Digital Technologies
subjects.description: Master essential computing, internet safety, and foundational algorithmic thinking.

topics.title: Introduction to Computer Systems
topics.summary: Understand hardware, software, and basic safe computing practices.
objectives: Identify input and output hardware devices.
Understand the role of operating systems.
Practice safe internet navigation habits.
topics.lesson: A computer system consists of hardware (physical components you can touch) and software (programs and instructions that tell hardware what to do).
topics.example: A keyboard and mouse are input devices, a monitor and printer are output devices.

questions.q: Which of the following is an input device?
questions.explain: A keyboard allows data entry into the computer system.
